theory: The intro and large-trial fact confuse counts with proportions: observed counts need not become closer to expected counts as trials increase, whereas observed proportions usually become closer to theoretical probabilities. Replace the blanket claim that variation does not mean unfairness with the qualified statement that variation alone does not establish unfairness; the source explicitly allows unusually large discrepancies to raise suspicion.
